models.name: shopping_mall_seller_compliance_documents
models.description:
Documents submitted by sellers for compliance verification purposes.

Tracks all official documents sellers must submit as part of the approval process: business licenses, IDs, tax forms, etc. Each document is associated with a specific seller application and has a lifecycle from upload through review to approval or rejection. Currently stored as file references in the file system, not physically stored in the database.

Relationships: Linked to shopping_mall_seller_applications (via application_id) and referenced by shopping_mall_seller_profiles for compliance status.
Related to: shopping_mall_seller_applications (parent entity) and shopping_mall_admin_actions (audit trail of approvers).

foreignFields.name: application_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller application this document is associated with. {@link shopping_mall_seller_applications.id}

plainFields.name: document_type
plainFields.description: Type of document being submitted (e.g., 'business_license', 'government_id', 'tax_certificate', 'bank_statement').

plainFields.name: document_title
plainFields.description: User-provided title for this document (e.g., 'Business License - ABC Company').

plainFields.name: document_path
plainFields.description: URI path to the document file stored in cloud storage (e.g., 's3://bucket/seller-docs/uuid-file.pdf').

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original filename of this document as uploaded by the seller.

plainFields.name: file_size_bytes
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes, used for storage accounting.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/jpeg').

plainFields.name: file_hash
plainFields.description: SHA-256 hash of the file content, used for integrity verification.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current review status of this document ('uploaded', 'reviewed', 'approved', 'rejected').

plainFields.name: review_notes
plainFields.description: Notes from admins regarding the review of this document.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller uploaded this document.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the document was reviewed by an admin.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the document was approved by an admin.

plainFields.name: rejected_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the document was rejected by an admin.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this compliance document record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this compliance document record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this compliance document record was logically deleted (soft delete). Null indicates active record.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_sales_analytics
models.description:
Aggregated sales performance data for each approved seller on the platform.

Stores pre-calculated sales metrics and analytics derived from order transactions. These metrics are updated asynchronously by background jobs based on payment records and order status changes. This table is denormalized for performance optimization and contains no business rules for transactional modifications, only read-only data used for seller dashboards and reporting.

Relationships: References shopping_mall_seller for ownership. Created from aggregation of shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items.
Related to: shopping_mall_order_items (source data for calculations).

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller whose sales data is being aggregated. {@link shopping_mall_seller.id}

plainFields.name: total_orders
plainFields.description: Total number of completed orders placed by all customers for this seller's products.

plainFields.name: total_revenue
plainFields.description: Total revenue generated from sales (sum of all order item totals before platform commission).

plainFields.name: total_units_sold
plainFields.description: Total number of product units sold across all orders for this seller.

plainFields.name: average_order_value
plainFields.description: Average value of completed orders for this seller, calculated as total_revenue / total_orders.

plainFields.name: best_selling_product_id
plainFields.description: ID of the product variant with the highest sales volume. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: best_selling_product_name
plainFields.description: Name of the best-selling product variant for this seller.

plainFields.name: best_selling_product_quantity
plainFields.description: Total quantity sold of the best-selling product variant.

plainFields.name: best_selling_product_revenue
plainFields.description: Total revenue generated by the best-selling product variant.

plainFields.name: last_updated
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this analytics record was last updated by the background job.

plainFields.name: time_period_start
plainFields.description: Start date of the time period covered by this aggregation (e.g., last 30 days).

plainFields.name: time_period_end
plainFields.description: End date of the time period covered by this aggregation (e.g., last 30 days).

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_inventory_alerts
models.description:
Automatic inventory threshold alerts generated for sellers when stock falls below defined levels.

System-generated notifications triggered by inventory monitoring jobs that scan product variants and compare their stock levels against configured thresholds (5% and 1% of original stock). Alerts are sent through email and in-app notifications to help sellers manage replenishment.

Relationships: Associated with shopping_mall_product_variants (through variant_id) and linked to shopping_mall_seller via owner relationship.
Related to: shopping_mall_product_variants (source of inventory data).

foreignFields.name: variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant that triggered this inventory alert. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who owns this product variant. {@link shopping_mall_seller.id}

plainFields.name: inventory_level
plainFields.description: Current inventory count of the product variant at the time the alert was triggered.

plainFields.name: original_stock
plainFields.description: Original stock quantity set when the variant was created (used to calculate percentage thresholds).

plainFields.name: alert_type
plainFields.description: Type of alert triggered ('low_stock_5_percent' or 'low_stock_1_percent').

plainFields.name: product_name
plainFields.description: Name of the product associated with the affected variant.

plainFields.name: variant_attributes
plainFields.description: JSON string representing the variant attributes (e.g., {"color":"red","size":"large"}).

plainFields.name: triggered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this inventory threshold was breached and the alert was generated.

plainFields.name: escalated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the alert was escalated (5% alert triggered and then 1% alert triggered later).

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the inventory level was replenished above the respective threshold.

plainFields.name: notified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the notification (email, in-app) was successfully delivered to the seller.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this alert record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this alert record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this alert record was logically deleted (soft delete). Null indicates active record.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_actions
models.description:
Records all actions performed by administrators on the system.

Captures a log of every administrative operation, such as user suspension, product deletion, order override, or refund approval. Each action is tied to an admin and an affected entity (e.g., a user, order, or product). This table serves as the primary audit trail for accountability.

Action types include: SUSPEND_USER, APPROVE_SELLER, DELETE_PRODUCT, OVERRIDE_INVENTORY, APPROVE_REFUND, etc.

This table is immutable — once recorded, entries never change. No soft delete capability is provided because administrative history is legally required to be preserved.

References the shopping_mall_admin table to identify the acting admin, and various other tables (shopping_mall_customer, shopping_mall_seller, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_products) to identify the target of the action.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed this action. {@link shopping_mall_admin.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of action performed. Examples: SUSPEND_USER, APPROVE_SELLER, DELETE_PRODUCT, OVERRIDE_INVENTORY, APPROVE_REFUND, REJECT_REVIEW, UPDATE_CONFIG. Must be one of the predefined administrative actions supported by the system.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity affected by the action. Example values: 'customer', 'seller', 'order', 'product', 'review', 'config'. Determines which table contains the target_id reference.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of the affected entity (e.g., shopping_mall_customer.id, shopping_mall_orders.id, etc.). The meaning depends on target_entity_type.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Explanation provided by the admin for performing this action. Used for audit trail and compliance review. May include comments like 'Fraud detected' or 'Violation of TOS'.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: JSON string containing additional contextual data about the action (e.g., old/new values, specific parameters changed). Stored as text for flexibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action was recorded. Always set by the system and immutable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when this record was last modified. In this table, this will always equal created_at since entries are immutable.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs
models.description:
Comprehensive system-wide audit trail capturing all critical system events involving administrators.

Records detailed system events related to administrative activities, such as config changes, login attempts, permission changes, or security alerts. This table is more granular than admin_actions and logs internal system responses to admin behavior (e.g., attempted privilege escalation).

Used for forensic analysis after security incidents or compliance investigations. Every entry ties back to an admin session or authentication context.

References shopping_mall_admin for identity and shopping_mall_admin_sessions for session context. Ensures complete accountability by logging both direct actions and system-detected anomalies.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator associated with this audit event. {@link shopping_mall_admin.id}.

foreignFields.name: session_id
foreignFields.description: The admin session during which the event occurred. {@link shopping_mall_admin_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of audit event. Examples: ADMIN_LOGIN, PERMISSION_CHANGE, CONFIG_UPDATE, PRIVILEGE_GRANT, SESSION_TERMINATED, FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPT, EXTERNAL_API_ERROR.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Criticality level of the audit event. Values: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL. Determines alerting behavior and urgency for review.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the admin performed the action that triggered this audit log.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser or client user agent string used by the admin during this event.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Structured JSON string with detailed context for the audit event. May include old/new values, error codes, or stack traces used for debugging.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time when the audit event was generated by the system. Always set automatically.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when this audit record was last modified. Always equals created_at since entries are immutable.

models.name: shopping_mall_system_configurations
models.description:
Central configuration store for system-wide operational parameters.

Defines global settings that are shared across all users and components, such as tax rates, payment gateway preferences, email templates, pricing cap settings, and notification thresholds. Minimizes hardcoding and enables dynamic system behavior without deployments.

Each configuration is a key-value pair with an optionally scoped context (e.g., 'default', 'US', 'EUR'). Values are stored as JSON strings to handle complex structured data.

This table is managed exclusively by admins and is referenced by multiple microservices during runtime for configuration resolution.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who last modified this configuration entry. {@link shopping_mall_admin.id}.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key. Must be unique across the entire system. Format: domain.field.example (e.g., 'payment.gateway', 'email.template.order_confirmation', 'pricing.max_seller_price').

plainFields.name: environment
plainFields.description: Configuration scope or environment. Examples: 'default', 'production', 'staging', 'US', 'EU'. Used for environment-specific or region-specific overrides. Defaults to 'default'.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: JSON-formatted string containing the configuration value. Supports strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and objects. Example: '{"enabled": true, "fee_percent": 0.08}'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable explanation of what this configuration controls. Used by admin users to understand purpose. Example: 'Platform-wide transaction fee percentage applied to all sales.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last modified.

models.name: shopping_mall_global_settings
models.description:
Global system-wide operational settings that define the platform's behavior.

Contains non-configurable, core platform-wide policies governed by legal, compliance, and security requirements. Unlike system_configurations (which are dynamic and reconfigurable), these values are typically hard-bound and require legal review to change.

Examples: GDPR retention periods, payment dispute window limits, refund eligibility duration, maximum file size upload, or admin session timeout levels.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who last modified this global setting. {@link shopping_mall_admin.id}.

plainFields.name: setting_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the setting, using dot-notation for hierarchy. Examples: 'compliance.refund_period_days', 'security.max_session_duration_minutes', 'upload.max_image_size_mb'.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Value of the setting, stored as string for compatibility. For numeric values: '14'. For boolean: 'true'. For thresholds: '500'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Explanation of this setting, its legal or business rationale, and consequences of change. Example: 'Maximum number of days a customer can request a refund after delivery. Based on GDPR and local consumer laws.'

plainFields.name: is_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this setting is currently active in the system. Used for toggling policies on/off without deletion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Date and time when this global setting was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Date and time when this global setting was last modified.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_notifications
models.description:
Management of notification triggers and rules for administrators.

Defines which administrative actions should trigger automated email or dashboard alerts (e.g., suspicious login, failed payment, high-risk refund request). Ensures that only critical events surface to the Admin Dashboard to prevent alert fatigue.

Each record specifies an event type from system_internal_observations, a target group (e.g., 'pending_admins', 'all_admins'), and whether the notification is enabled.

Allows admins to customize their alerting preferences for compliance, security, and operational monitoring.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who created or modified this notification rule. {@link shopping_mall_admin.id}.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Event type that triggers this notification. Examples: 'ADMIN_LOGIN_FROM_NEW_DEVICE', 'HIGH_RISK_ORDER', 'SPAMMY_REVIEW', 'TOP_SELLER_SUSPENDED'. Must correspond to system-generated event types in audit logs.

plainFields.name: notification_channel
plainFields.description: How the notification is delivered. Values: 'email', 'dashboard_alert', 'sms', or 'all'.

plainFields.name: target_group
plainFields.description: Group of admins who receive this notification. Examples: 'all_admins', 'finance_team', 'security_team', 'support_lead'.

plainFields.name: is_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this notification rule is active. Useful for temporarily disabling non-critical alerts during system maintenance.

plainFields.name: threshold
plainFields.description: Optional numerical threshold. For example: 'Trigger notification after 3 failed login attempts within 10 minutes'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of what this notification is intended to help the admin detect or respond to.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time when this notification rule was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Time when this notification rule was last modified.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_dashboard_configs
models.description:
Personalized configuration for each admin's dashboard interface and display preferences.

Stores user-specific UI preferences such as which widgets to show, their order, default date ranges for analytics, chart types, and notification visibility level. Respects individual workflow styles while maintaining system-wide data integrity.

Each admin has one and only one dashboard configuration record. Changes are applied immediately to the user's active session upon next page load.

Only editable by the admin themselves or by senior admins for troubleshooting.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator this configuration belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_admin.id}.

plainFields.name: widgets
plainFields.description: JSON array defining which dashboard widgets are visible and their order. Example: ["order_volume", "admin_actions_count", "recent_seller_approvals"]. Every admin must have at least one widget.

plainFields.name: default_timeframe
plainFields.description: Default time range for analytics charts. Values: '7d', '30d', '90d', 'ytd'.

plainFields.name: theme
plainFields.description: User-selected UI theme. Values: 'light', 'dark', 'auto'.

plainFields.name: notification_level
plainFields.description: How noisy notifications are for this admin. Values: 'high', 'medium', 'low'. High = show all alerts. Low = show only CRITICAL events.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Date and time when this configuration was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Date and time when this configuration was last modified.

models.name: shopping_mall_notifications
models.description:
Main notification records generated by system events or admin actions.

Represents individual notification messages triggered by business events such as order status changes, review replies, or inventory alerts. Each notification is queued for delivery and may have one or more recipients. Notifications store the template used, subject, content, priority, and delivery status.

Notifications are created by system processes (e.g., order fulfillment completes) or admin actions (e.g., broadcast announcement). Notifications persist for audit purposes even if delivery fails and are marked as archived if outdated.

Each notification may have multiple recipients via shopping_mall_notification_recipients. Delivery outcomes are tracked in shopping_mall_notification_delivery_logs.

Soft delete is supported to preserve audit history while allowing logical removal from active views.

foreignFields.name: notification_template_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the template used for this notification. {@link shopping_mall_notification_templates.id}.

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description: The subject line of the notification email or push notification message. May be overridden per recipient via template variables but stored here as resolved static value.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The full body content of the notification. May be rendered HTML for email or plain text for SMS. Generated by resolving template variables against recipient context.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Priority level of the notification. Determines delivery urgency: 'low', 'normal', 'high', 'critical'. Critical notifications bypass rate limits.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current delivery state of this notification: 'pending', 'scheduled', 'sending', 'sent', 'failed', 'archived'. Pending means queued for processing; sent means at least one recipient received it.

plainFields.name: trigger_event
plainFields.description: Source event that triggered this notification (e.g., 'order_shipped', 'review_submitted', 'admin_broadcast'). Used for analytics and system debugging.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification record was created in the system. Always non-null.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this notification record. Updated when status changes or retry occurs.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification was logically deleted (soft delete). Null if active. Used for audit trails and filtering active notifications.

models.name: shopping_mall_notification_templates
models.description:
Pre-defined notification templates used to generate standardized messages.

Templates serve as reusable message blueprints for common business events such as order confirmations, password resets, and product reviews. Each template includes a subject pattern and content body with placeholders (e.g., {{customer_name}}, {{order_id}}).

Templates are managed exclusively by admins via the admin dashboard. They support versioning through single active version; each update creates a new record with the same template_id but a higher version number. Template_id is preserved across versions for logical grouping.

Fields are static and rarely updated—changes require admin approval and versioning to ensure historical notifications remain unchanged.

Template content may include dynamic variables that resolve at delivery time using context from the trigger event and recipient.

plainFields.name: template_id
plainFields.description: Human-readable identifier for the template type (e.g., 'order_shipped', 'password_reset'). Used for programmatic lookup. Must be unique across all versions.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Version number of this template (e.g., 1, 2, 3). Higher versions supersede older ones. The latest version with the same template_id is the active one for new notifications.

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description: Subject line template with placeholders like {{customer_name}}; will be resolved before delivery. Supports variable interpolation.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full message body template with HTML or plain text and variables. Supports conditional logic (e.g., {% if seller %}...{% endif %}).

plainFields.name: channel
plainFields.description: Delivery channel this template is designed for: 'email', 'sms', 'in_app'. Determines render format and delivery method.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this template version is active and available for new notifications. Only one version per template_id should be active at a time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this template version was created. For historical tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this template version was last updated. Updated on every change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this template version was logically deleted. Null if active. Used for audit trails and restores.

models.name: shopping_mall_notification_recipients
models.description:
Links notifications to their intended recipients and stores channel-specific delivery details.

This table bridges notifications (shopping_mall_notifications) with recipient actors (shopping_mall_customer, shopping_mall_seller, shopping_mall_admin). Each notification can have multiple recipients, and each recipient entry stores destination information like email, phone number, or device token.

Recipient addresses are pulled from authoritative actor tables at time of notification creation and stored here for consistency—even if the actor changes their contact info later. This ensures notifications are delivered to the address as it existed when the notification was triggered.

Recipient entries are managed indirectly via the notification system and never directly edited by end users.

foreignFields.name: notification_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the notification this recipient is associated with. {@link shopping_mall_notifications.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer recipient, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_customer.id}. Optional: null if recipient is not a customer.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller recipient, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_seller.id}. Optional: null if recipient is not a seller.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the admin recipient, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_admin.id}. Optional: null if recipient is not an admin.

plainFields.name: recipient_type
plainFields.description: Type of the recipient actor: 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'. Determines which ID field (customer_id, seller_id, admin_id) is populated.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address of the recipient at the time of notification creation. Copied from the actor's profile to ensure consistency even if the user changes email later.

plainFields.name: phone
plainFields.description: Phone number of the recipient at the time of notification creation, in E.164 format. Copied from actor profile for SMS delivery. Null if not used for this notification.

plainFields.name: device_token
plainFields.description: Push notification token (e.g., Firebase token) for in-app notifications. Null if in-app delivery is not used for this recipient.

plainFields.name: channel
plainFields.description: How the recipient prefers to receive this notification: 'email', 'sms', 'in_app', or 'all'. Can override template default channel.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of this recipient's delivery: 'pending', 'sent', 'failed', 'unsubscribed'. Determines retry behavior and delivery status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this recipient record was created alongside the notification.

models.name: shopping_mall_notification_delivery_logs
models.description:
Detailed logs of each attempted delivery of a notification to a recipient.

This table provides an audit trail of every delivery attempt, success, failure, and retry. Each entry corresponds to one delivery attempt for one recipient under one notification.

Logs capture admin and system actions including retry counts, error codes, timestamps, and server responses. This allows for debugging, compliance, and analytics on delivery reliability.

This is a subsidiary table: not directly accessed by users, only used internally by the system and admin dashboard to track delivery health.

foreignFields.name: notification_recipient_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the recipient record this log belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_notification_recipients.id}.

plainFields.name: attempt_number
plainFields.description: Sequential number of this delivery attempt: 1 for first try, 2 for retry, etc. Used for logging and backoff strategies.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Final outcome of this attempt: 'queued', 'attempting', 'sent', 'failed', 'bounced', 'rejected'. Failed cases include timeouts, authentication failures, invalid addresses.

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: Error code returned by the delivery service (e.g., 'email_invalid', 'sms_limit_exceeded', 'api_timeout'). Null if successful.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Detailed human-readable error message from the third-party service or internal system. Used for debugging and support.

plainFields.name: delivery_service
plainFields.description: Service provider used for this delivery: 'sendgrid', 'twilio', 'firebase', 'internal_email'.

plainFields.name: response_headers
plainFields.description: Raw HTTP headers returned by the external service for this attempt. Stored as JSON string for debugging purposes.

plainFields.name: response_body
plainFields.description: Raw HTTP response body returned by the external service for this attempt. Stored as JSON string for debugging purposes.

plainFields.name: sent_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attempt was successfully sent to the external service (e.g., when API call was made).

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the external service confirmed delivery to the recipient. Only set for 'sent' or 'delivered' outcomes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this log entry was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this log entry was last updated (e.g., status changed from attempting to failed).

models.name: shopping_mall_notification_schedules
models.description:
Stores scheduled delivery requests for notifications that should be sent at a future date and time.

Used for non-immediate notifications such as daily summaries, weekly sales reports, scheduled reminders, or delivery notifications timed for business hours. This table allows the system to decouple notification generation from delivery timing.

Schedules are automatically consumed by a background job that checks for pending schedules every minute. Upon firing, the system creates a corresponding shopping_mall_notification and its recipients.

This table is critical for delayed delivery workflows but is managed entirely by the system or admin—end users never interact with it directly.

foreignFields.name: notification_template_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the template that will be used when this schedule triggers. {@link shopping_mall_notification_templates.id}.

plainFields.name: scheduled_for
plainFields.description: The exact time this notification should be triggered and delivered. Must be in the future. Once hit, system creates the notification and deletes this schedule.

plainFields.name: recipient_filter
plainFields.description: JSON string describing which actors should receive this scheduled notification. Example: '{"role": "customer", "last_order_after": "2025-11-01"}'. Used to dynamically determine recipients at trigger time.

plainFields.name: context_data
plainFields.description: JSON string with key-value variables to inject into template during processing (e.g., '{"sales_period": "Q4 2025"}'). Expands template placeholders at delivery time.

plainFields.name: trigger_event
plainFields.description: Event name that will be logged in the resulting notification (e.g., 'weekly_report_sent', 'reminder_alert').

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the schedule: 'pending', 'fired', 'cancelled', 'expired'. Fired means succeeded; cancelled means manually stopped; expired means scheduled_for has passed without firing.

plainFields.name: max_retries

models.name: shopping_mall_issues
models.description:
Main entity representing issue reports from any actor type (customer or seller). Holds shared attributes and tracks the actor type.

This is the central record for all issue reporting within the platform. It acts as a polymorphic container that relates to either a customer or seller through their respective subtype tables. This design ensures referential integrity at the database level, preventing ambiguous or invalid actor states (e.g., both actors set, neither actor set).

The actor_type field explicitly identifies whether the issue originates from a customer or seller. This enables efficient querying and filtering by actor type without any nullable fields. All shared issue metadata (title, body, status) resides here, while actor-specific contextual data (like sessions) is stored in the subtype entities.

This table is a primary entity because administrators and customers may directly view, filter, and manage issues from the platform interface, regardless of the actor type that reported them. It is referenced by the two subtype tables with 1:1 relationships.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: The type of actor who reported this issue. Must be either 'customer' or 'seller'. This field enables the polymporphic pattern and replaces the need for multiple nullable foreign keys.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Concise summary of the reported issue. Often used as a subject line for notifications and internal triaging.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the issue provided by the reporting actor. May include screenshots, timestamps, or contextual details about what occurred.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the issue report. Valid values: 'pending', 'under_review', 'resolved', 'rejected'. New issues start as 'pending'. Admins update the status as they process.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the issue was first created and reported. This is immutable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when any field in this record was last modified. Typically updated when status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If null, the issue is active. When set, the issue is considered archived and hidden from active views.

models.name: shopping_mall_issue_of_customers
models.description:
Subtype entity holding customer-specific contextual data linked to issues reported by customers.

This table extends the main shopping_mall_issues entity with data specific to customer-reported issues, including the customer ID and their session at the time of reporting. This design replaces a nullable customer_id field in the main table, enforcing referential integrity and allowing the database to guarantee that every issue of this subtype is linked to exactly one valid customer.

Each record in this table has a 1:1 relationship with exactly one record in shopping_mall_issues. The same issue cannot be linked to both a customer and a seller. Customer-specific session data is stored here to provide context for the issue (e.g., device, location), which may be different from seller context.

This table is subsidiary because it is always accessed through the main shopping_mall_issues entity and is not directly managed by users via API endpoints. It is managed automatically by the system when a customer reports an issue.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_issue_id
foreignFields.description: The main issue this customer-specific report belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_issues.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who reported this issue. {@link shopping_mall_customer.id}. This field is non-nullable to enforce integrity.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_session_id
foreignFields.description: The customer's active session ID at the time the issue was reported. {@link shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id}. Provides context about the user's device, IP, and environment.

models.name: shopping_mall_issue_of_sellers
models.description:
Subtype entity holding seller-specific contextual data linked to issues reported by sellers.

This table extends the main shopping_mall_issues entity with data specific to seller-reported issues, including the seller ID and their session at the time of reporting. This design replaces a nullable seller_id field in the main table, enforcing referential integrity and allowing the database to guarantee that every issue of this subtype is linked to exactly one valid seller.

Each record in this table has a 1:1 relationship with exactly one record in shopping_mall_issues. The same issue cannot be linked to both a seller and a customer. Seller-specific session data is stored here for accountability and audit purposes.

This table is subsidiary because it is always accessed through the main shopping_mall_issues entity and is not directly managed by users via API endpoints. It is created automatically by the system when a seller reports an issue.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_issue_id
foreignFields.description: The main issue this seller-specific report belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_issues.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who reported this issue. {@link shopping_mall_seller.id}. This field is non-nullable to enforce integrity.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_session_id
foreignFields.description: The seller's active session ID at the time the issue was reported. {@link shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id}. Provides context about the seller's device, IP, and environment, which is critical for fraud detection and dispute resolution.
